Planned comparisons were run to test the experimental
hypothesis. T-tests showed significantly fewer ditransitive responses and more dative responses after dative prime
than after either ditransitive (p < .01 for both subjects &
items) or provide-with primes (p < .05) but no difference
in the percentage of ditransitive responses after ditransitive
and provide-with primes (p > .1).
Finally, we tested whether there was a significant difference between ditransitive and prepostional object responses following an intransitive prime. In the items
analysis the ditransitive mean was 56% , while the prepositional object was 44% . This difference is not significant (p > 1) confirming that Bock's finding of no independent preference for either clause type was also true of
our items. Although in the subjects analysis the difference
was larger, again it did not reach significance (p =.092).
W e will return to this point in the general discussion.

decisions.reason: Recovered Bock & Loebell (1990, 10.1016/0010-0277(90)90035-i; pubmed.raw, 39-page PDF, original.pdftotext.txt) shows that while pp. 17 and 35-36 acknowledge locative/beneficiary goal overlap (addressed via Experiment 2's passive/locative test) and allow thematic linking to grammatical roles before constituent formation (Bock et al., 1989/1992), the original explicitly claimed for the explored oblique-phrase domain that predicate/constituent structures ('[NP [V NP PP]]' vs. '[NP [V NP NP]]') are 'devoid of thematic content' and 'insulated from the elaboration of constituents' (p. 35), so event-structure changes do not alter phrase-structure persistence (Abstract, Experiment 1). Also, the intransitive baseline cited by Hare & Goldberg traces to Bock (1986, Experiment 1; 1990 pp. 16-17), not a tested 1990 condition, and original locative, passive/by-locative, and infinitive controls were not rerun. In Hare & Goldberg (f4ef4cba54e4ea6b.txt), the retested Experiment 1 ditransitive vs. prepositional-dative contrast replicates (87% vs. 55% ditransitive responses, 32% difference, p<.01 for subjects and items), and the authors affirm that syntactic form contributes alongside semantics (not 'statistically_successful_but_flawed'). However, pitting '[NP V NP PP]' syntax against '<agent, recipient, theme>' role order in 'provide-with' primes yields 83% ditransitives (p<.05 vs. dative, p>.1 vs. ditransitive, ruling out simple additive animacy), disconfirming thematic-role-independent '[NP V NP PP]' phrase-structure priming ('The structural prime only has an effect only when it combines both the syntax and the semantics of the prepositional dative', p. 210), supporting 'mixed'.
